title: Earth Jukebox

pointEmpty: Click or tap the globe to select a point.
overlayError: Could not display the map for {period} (the data is still available to listen to/query).
unitsEquivalenceNote: Temperature anomalies in K and in degrees Celsius have the same magnitude (they are temperature differences, not absolute temperatures).
peruIntro: Pick a place to see its story, listen to it, and compare the GISTEMP anomaly of the nearest cell.
peruCellPending: Select this place on the map or with the button above to see its cell value.
peruCellValueLabel: GISTEMP anomaly at the nearest cell
accessibleIntro: This path works fully with keyboard and screen reader, and does not depend on the 3D globe.
accessibleInvalidCoords: Invalid coordinates: latitude must be between -90 and 90, and longitude between -180 and 180.
accessibleNoCell: There is no data cell for this point yet.
accessibleValueMissingLine: Anomaly: no data in this cell for this period.
accessibleMeaningNote: The anomaly shows how far temperature deviates from the baseline average, not an absolute temperature.
accessibleAudioMutedLine: Audio: silence you chose (mute is on).
shareErrorVersion: The preset in the link is an unknown version ({version}).
shareErrorTooLong: The preset link is too long.
shareErrorFields: The preset in the link has invalid data: {fields}.
shareErrorGeneric: Could not read the preset from the link.
shareErrorDataVersion: The preset in the link was created with a different data version ({field}); the data may have changed since then.
shareLocalNote: This link only opens in this browser/device unless you deploy the app (it does not mean another device on your network can open it).
accessibleNarrationAutoLabel: Navigation voice: announce every confirmed change by voice (off by default; not recommended with a screen reader)
djIntro: Mix temperature (GISTEMP), rain (NASA POWER) and sea ice (NOAA/NSIDC G02135, 2023) of the selected point over a shared pulse. Requires enabling sound above.
compositionExplain: Listen to a {seconds} s piece (8 bars at 96 BPM) with three synthesized instruments: soft piano (temperature), drops (rain) and a crystalline pad (ice). It is not a real acoustic piano. It never starts by itself.
compositionRules: Rules: temperature raises or lowers the register of the same motif (C-D-E-G-A); rain adds drops on the pulse without changing the tempo; ice gives one soft chord per bar with volume equal to its fraction. No data means that instrument is silent; ice 0 is silence and rain 0 is zero drops.
compositionStatusPlaying: Playing the {seconds} s composition. New data enters at the next bar; a null value silences that instrument immediately.
soundingNothing: No instrument is sounding: there is no real data for this point and period.
soundingIceZero: Ice: real 0% (silence, below the detection threshold).
musicRangeNote: Fixed musical range from {min} to +{max} °C (music version 2), the same for every point and period; it differs from the legend color range (-5 to +5 °C). The scale has 16 registers: close values may sound the same, the real value is shown above.
musicSaturated: The {value} °C anomaly exceeds the musical range: the sound saturates at the extreme, but the displayed value is the real one.
shareErrorMusicVersion: The link uses an unknown music version ({version}); it is not played so as not to claim it sounds the same.
shareLegacyMusic: Note: this link comes from the previous music version (linear -5 to +5 scale). The current music uses a different mapping and may sound different; the data are the same.
djNoPoint: Select a point on the globe or in Accessible to mix its data.
djRainLoading: Loading NASA POWER rain for this point...
djRainApi: Rain: live NASA POWER query (MERRA-2), year {year}.
djRainError: Could not get rain data for this point (network/CORS). Only locally available points are used.
djRainSaturated: Rain value outside the 0-20 mm/day musical range: visually saturated.
djUnitsNote: PRECTOTCORR = monthly average of the daily rate (mm/day), MERRA-2 reanalysis, NOT a monthly total.
djDataVersionMismatch: Note: this data arrived with a different version than the opened shared link; it may have changed since then.
djIceLoading: Loading NOAA/NSIDC sea ice for this point...
djIceError: Could not get sea ice data for this point (network/validation).
djIceOutOfSeries: Period {period}: outside the real available series (2023 only); not extrapolated, no data.
djIceValue: Period {period}: {percent}% ice concentration (fraction of valid ocean area).
djIceValueMissing: Period {period}: no data (land, coast, pole-hole, or no valid ocean coverage in this cell).
djIceCoverage: Coverage: {count} real 25 km pixels averaged into this 2° cell.
djIceSource: Source: NOAA/NSIDC G02135 "Sea Ice Index" v4.0, 2023 data derived from NSIDC-0051 (NASA Team algorithm, through Dec. 2024; NSIDC-0803, also NASA Team, from Jan. 2025); not a pure NASA dataset.
djIceThresholdNote: G02135 sets pixel values below the 15% detection threshold to 0: a 0 (or a low aggregate) does not prove ice is absolutely absent.
djIceExploreTitle: Explore hemispheres (real points with verified coverage)
eicIntro: Official NASA SVS annual map paired with the GLOBAL ANNUAL indicator of the same year/dataset/baseline. Does not replace the local monthly mode.
eicRevisionWarning: GISTEMP may revise this value later; see the source for detail.
eicImageError: Could not load the remote annual map image.
historyIntro: Choose a place and the month and year you were born. We compare that month's temperature anomaly with the latest real month available, and you can listen to both, one after the other.
historyPlaceHelp: Type at least 2 letters (for example, Iquitos) and press Search. The search runs in your browser. If your town is missing, pick a point on the globe or type coordinates in the Accessible tab and use the button below.
historyUseGlobe: Use the point selected on the globe
historyBirthNote: Month and year you were born, from {min}. The day is not needed: these are monthly observations, not the exact weather of that day.
historyLatestNote: Latest real month available in this GISTEMP data: {period} (not "today").
historyCatalogError: The city catalog could not be loaded. You can pick a point on the globe or type coordinates in the Accessible tab.
historySearchNone: No results for "{q}". Try another name or pick a point on the globe.
historySearchCount: {total} results; showing the {shown} largest. Refine your search if yours is not listed.
historyPlaceChosen: Chosen place: {label} ({coords}). The data is one GISTEMP cell of 2° smoothed up to 1200 km: it describes a wide area, not just the city.
historyPlaceNone: You have not chosen a place yet.
historyErrNoPlace: Choose a place: search for a city or use the globe point.
historyErrEmpty: Enter the month and year you were born.
historyErrInvalid: The year must have 4 digits and the month must be valid.
historyErrBefore: The data starts in {min}. Choose a date from then on.
historyErrAfter: That date is later than the latest real month available ({max}).
historyErrNotAvailable: There is no data for that month in the package.
historyLoadError: The data for those months could not be loaded. Please try again.
historyGridMismatch: The two months do not share the same grid; no comparison is shown.
historySourceMismatch: The two months come from different sources; no comparison is shown.
historySharedBadPeriod: The story link uses a period that does not exist in this data.
historyStoryA: In {period}, the temperature anomaly at this place was {x} °C relative to the {baseline} average.
historyStoryMissingA: In {period} there is no data in this cell (No data); no value is made up.
historyStoryMissingB: In {period} there is no data in this cell (No data); no value is made up.
historyStorySame: It is the same month, so the difference is {d} °C.
historyStoryNoDelta: The difference is not available because one of the two values is missing.
historyCaveat: This is one monthly observation of a {deg}° cell smoothed up to {km} km, relative to the reference average: it is not the temperature of the day and does not by itself show a trend or a cause.
historyPlayingLoading: Showing that epoch on the globe before listening…
historyEpochError: That epoch could not be shown on the globe, so nothing is playing. Please try again.
historyStartError: The sound could not start. Please try again.
historyEnded: Finished. You can repeat or listen to the other epoch.
historyAudioOff: To listen, first press "Activate sound" in the audio bar above.
historyMuted: Sound is muted: unmute it in the audio bar to listen.
historyNoDataListen: This epoch has no data; there is no music for it.
historySpeechUnsupported: Your browser has no speech voice; the text above is the full story.
historyAnnounceNoData: {period}: no data in this cell; there is no music for this month.
historyVoiceLabel: Announce each epoch by voice (optional; the text is always shown)
historySpeak: Listen to the story with voice
historyHowTo: Each month plays as a short 20-second piece with the same motif, tempo, volume and seed. Only the anomaly changes: the higher it is, the higher the notes sound.
historyVariability: A single month changes a lot from year to year; only many years together show a long-term trend. This comparison does not show a trend or a cause.
historyQuestion1: Guiding question: what changed in the notes between before and after?
historyQuestion2: Guiding question: what data is missing to draw a conclusion?
historyMissing: Not shown: the exact weather of a day, absolute temperature, other months and years at the same place, or causes. Try another month or another place.
historyPrivacy: The link from "Save and generate link" includes the place (coordinates) and the two compared months, not your name, age or exact day. Nothing is saved automatically.
historyDetailsSummary: See the data and how to read it
historyShortNote: These are monthly anomalies for a wide area, not the exact weather of the day nor proof of a trend or cause.
djCaptionTemperature: Piano: the anomaly raises or lowers the register.
djCaptionRain: Drops: the month's rain adds drops over the pulse.
djCaptionIce: Soft chord: its volume is the ice fraction.
